title: Green solvent-mediated extraction of biomolecules: opportunities, advances, and future directions
content: The sustainable extraction of biomolecules has become an indispensable component of modern biomanufacturing, integrating the principles of green chemistry, biotechnology, and biorefinery to enable environmentally sustainable production. Driven by stringent regulatory requirements, an exponential growth in the use of green solvents (GS) has been observed for biomolecule extraction over the past decade. In this review, we present a comprehensive and critical discussion on the evolution of GS-based extraction technologies for the recovery of biomolecules from various natural feedstocks. In contrast to previous reviews, which were limited in scope, focusing on specific biomolecules or solvent classes, this review examines a broad spectrum of GSs (including water, bio-based solvents, molten salt hydrates, supercritical fluids, CO2-expanded liquids, switchable solvents, ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, supramolecular solvents, and liquid polymers) and biomolecule classes (including carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, alkaloids, phenolics, terpenoids, vitamins, and other high-value natural products), offering a wider perspective on developments in the field. Advancements based on performance parameters like extraction efficiency, selectivity, solvent recovery, toxicity, and scalability for major families of GSs along with discussions of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing solvent-biomolecule interactions, solvent polarity, hydrogen-bonding, viscosity, mass transfer, and solvent nanostructure are critically evaluated. Because favourable solvent properties do not by themselves ensure a greener process, particular attention is given to comparisons with conventional solvents, preservation of biomolecule quality, downstream product recovery and solvent regeneration, and representative techno-economic and life-cycle case studies, with greenness assessed at the process level rather than inferred from solvent origin. Furthermore, the integration of GSs with advanced extraction technologies, including ultrasound, microwave, and pressurised liquid-assisted extraction, is discussed, with particular emphasis placed on synergistic strategies that enhance extraction performance while reducing energy and solvent consumption. Finally, GS-based spin-offs, regulatory considerations, and key challenges including predictive solvent selection, process scale-up, and digital solvent discovery are critically assessed. Emerging opportunities offered by hybrid GS systems, machine learning-guided solvent design, integrated biorefineries, and omics-enabled extraction are also highlighted. Overall, a strategic roadmap is presented envisaging the development of GS-based next-generation extraction technologies and the emerging circular bioeconomy.
